text: Those in power always make room for someone wise and humble.
Do not praise or despise anyone on the basis of their looks.
The honeybee is very small, but it makes the sweetest food.
Don't boast about your clothes or act important when you are honored. Only the Lord does things truly worthy of praise, but he keeps them hidden from our sight.
Kings often lose their power to those who had seemed to be nobodies,
while honored rulers are captured and disgraced.
Find out the truth before you criticize.
Don't interrupt others— hear them out, then give your answer.
If it's none of your business, then don't argue with them, and stay away from sinners when they discuss what to do.
Students, don't let yourself become too busy. If you do, you will sin and not find success or escape trouble.
Some people work all day long as hard as they can, but they keep getting poorer.
Others are poor and weak; they work slowly and always need help. But the Lord shows kindness
and to everyone's surprise, he lifts them from poverty and gives them honor.
All things, whether good or bad, come from the Lord. He gives life and riches or takes them away.
The Lord gives wisdom by teaching us to understand his Law. He helps us love each other and do right.
Sinners are dishonest and live in darkness, proud of their evil from the day they are born, and so evil will stay with them until the day they die.[24]
But the Lord gives success to his faithful people and blesses them with gifts that last forever.
You can become rich, if you work hard and never spend any money. But then what?
When you finally retire to enjoy what you own, you soon may die, and then your wealth will belong to others.
When you agree to do work, stay busy and don't quit.
Don't be surprised at what sinners do; trust the Lord and keep working, because he can make you rich in a moment's time.
Suddenly, he will reward you and bless you with prosperity, if you are faithful to him. *
So don't say, “I already have everything I need— what more could the Lord do for me?
Nothing can harm me now!”
When people are well off, they never mention how needy they once were, and when they have trouble, the good times are forgotten.
But at the end of life, the Lord will pay us back for what we have done.
Pleasant memories fade after an hour of pain, but the way that you lived is made clear by how you die
and by what kind of children you leave behind. So don't praise anyone until they are dead.
Don't let just anyone come to your house. Dishonest people will trick you,
as bird hunters use decoys to trap quails. They watch you like spies, waiting for some mistake
or for a chance to make your good deeds seem evil.
One spark can start a fire, and one sinner's evil plan can end in murder.
Watch out for the schemes of those who do evil, or they may ruin your good name.
And if you let foreigners come to live in your home, they will cause trouble and persuade you to accept their customs and gods.[25]
